Any phone reads text aloud; proving the voice is a person costs. A seat is one voice on the town register: the applicant files a 90-second sample; the node keeps pitch, formant spacing and glottal pulse. Each epoch the holder reads the round's prompt (here opal, vertex, sonnet) and the epoch number into a new clip. A stored recording cannot name an epoch younger than itself, and a rented synthetic voice drifts on formants in minutes.

Fifty voices cost money: 25 dollars a clip, 300 a licensed sample chain, so a farm passes 15,000 before a clean week. A clerk knows a stranger by his cough.
